dedupe_keys.name: gridpack high performance electric grid simulation framework

description: GridPACK is an open-source framework and set of applications for simulating large electrical transmission grids on parallel, high-performance computers. It is developed at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory by Bruce Palmer, William Perkins, Yousu Chen, Renke Huang, Shrirang Abhyankar, Zhenyu Huang and others, to make fast grid simulation practical at very large scale. Prebuilt applications cover AC power flow, dynamic simulation, contingency analysis and state estimation, with dynamic security assessment and electromagnetic transient simulation under development, and the DOE CODE record also lists Kalman filter state estimation and real-time path rating. As a framework it provides modules for partitioning and distributing networks, custom bus and branch components, converting networks into algebraic equations, parallel solvers, task load balancing, input and output, contingency statistics, profiling and error handling. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitHub under a BSD 2-clause licence at no cost, with nine release tags and a latest commit in April 2026. Caveats: it targets C++ developers and parallel clusters, and some applications are not full-featured. Simulation uses are large-scale contingency screening, dynamic simulation and cascading outage analysis. Related records: platform-helics can couple it with other simulators.
interoperability: Usable as components in larger workflows
